classification.difficultyReason: Translate the enclosing and partition walls into a length constraint, combine it with the area and retain both valid dimension pairs.

content.prompt: A rectangular piece of land of area $5000\text{ m}^2$ is to be enclosed by a wall, and then divided into three equal regions by partition walls parallel to one of its sides. If the total length of the walls is $445\text{ m}$, calculate the possible dimensions of the land.

answer.short:
$62.5\text{ m}$ by $80\text{ m}$, or $160\text{ m}$ by $31.25\text{ m}$.

Count the two partition walls along with the enclosing walls before forming the quadratic.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the side length parallel to the two partition walls, and let the other side length be $y$ metres. There are four walls of length $x$ and two of length $y$.
$$\begin{align*}4x+2y&=445\\y&=\frac{445-4x}{2}\end{align*}$$
Using the area,
$$\begin{align*}xy&=5000\\\frac{x(445-4x)}{2}&=5000\\4x^2-445x+10000&=0\\(x-80)(4x-125)&=0\\x&=80\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{125}{4}.\end{align*}$$
When $x=80$, $y=\frac{(445-320)}{2}=62.5$. When $x=31.25$, $y=\frac{(445-125)}{2}=160$.

Both pairs have positive side lengths, area $5000\text{ m}^2$ and total wall length $445\text{ m}$. The possible dimensions are $62.5\text{ m}$ by $80\text{ m}$, or $160\text{ m}$ by $31.25\text{ m}$.
